rows: Think of a garden bed. Water one corner and the whole bed greens. Which corner are you watering?
Brawling is like compost. A little feeds the soil. Too much and nothing will grow.
A risk is like a loose fence post. It may hold, but I would not lean my weight on it.
Slow is like a seedling in spring. It takes patience, and I enjoy watching it.
The people come to the allotment for the crop. They should get something worth picking.
I have tended this patch for a while, and I know what it grows.
I am not the loudest plant in the bed, but I know my soil.
Look at the stance the way a gardener looks at a stem. Slow, and careful.
Technique is the mulch under everything. Which tool do you reach for when the plant droops?
Strikes are the heat in July. Too much and the leaves scorch. Where do you stop?
A risk without a fallback is like planting without a water butt. Who is watching the dry weather?
A stall is a bare patch left unplanted. Nobody gets a harvest from it.
The people have a right to a crop they can pick and taste. Let me show you the bed.
You call yourself among the best, the finest marrow on the stall. Let us see if it stands up to rain.
You are proud of your {strength}. Good, it is clearly well tended.
I have dug around your {strength} twice. It is sound, but it wants more compost.
Noted. You kept your head, which is how seedlings survive the frost.
Fair. We are looking at the same bed. Now let us see who does the weeding.
I could tell you what I think of your planting. I would rather let the crop speak.
One fall, one clean harvest. Keep me down and the plot is yours.
On the mat, every step is a turn of the spade. Keep up with me.
Grounded or standing, the spade still starts with the first grip.
Stay where you are and let me see what you are rooted in.
That answer is well rooted. It is more than I expected.
The bed still has no crop from you. It is going to seed.
Noted. I will take that seed and plant it.
Understood. It is a fair place to start the planting.
I will tend this match slowly and harvest it properly.
My approach is gentle and steady. I will show you the plot.
Whatever happens, you will know what went into the soil.
The crop is not ready yet. One more season to go.
I have one more row to plant. You will see it when the bell rings.
